question: Do actual residual-writeback and nextnorm SSE rank high-risk rows differently before any predictor is fitted?
hypotheses: If both rankings nearly coincide, changing the boundary alone offers little explanation at these finite scopes.
If rankings and cross-target captured losses disagree, scalar nextnorm risk is not interchangeable with residual-state fidelity; full downstream value remains unmeasured.
analysis: All72 saved scopes, fixed UB1 vs matched-prefix dense. No model, learned evaluator, weights, selector reconstruction, new labels or policy tuning. Compare scalar-label top7917 of31668 rows, tie-average Spearman, overlap, cross-target captured losses, per-source/step summaries.
limitations: Post-hoc scalar label ranking is descriptive; neither ranking is a deployable selector or a complete block/step/video causal objective.
